intent: Changed one variable: widened the sensor span from about ±0.024 m to ±0.03 m (spacing 15 mm), keeping the forward offset at 0.05 m, the 12 mm footprints, and all body and wheel values. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and max_error staying under 0.06 m, so runs reach further along the course. Under consideration without commitment: a shorter forward offset of about 0.03 m if steering_oscillation rises at speed after the span change. I would test that next as a separate change.
learning: Baseline evidence: all 60 trials went off track at about 0.10 to 0.15 progress, with one line-loss event each and max_error at the 0.06 m limit. Next iteration: if line_loss_events falls and progress rises, keep the wider span and test the forward offset. If line loss persists, the sensors may need to be wider still or the footprint larger, and I will check whether the loss happens on the sharp bends in the slalom.
rationale: The baseline (iteration 0) scored 54.37 and every trial in all three development tracks ended off track at about 10 to 15 percent progress. Each run recorded one line-loss event, and max_error sat at about 0.062 to 0.064 m, right at the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot therefore loses the tape once, drifts past the edge of the limit, and ends the run early. rms_error (0.02 to 0.028 m) and steering_oscillation (0.10 to 0.14) are modest, so the failure is an abrupt loss of the line, not sustained jitter at speed. That points at sensing coverage rather than the forward offset. With the current span of about ±0.024 m, the outer sensors can lose the 25 mm tape when it moves toward the edge of the array, which the Integrator's suggested first change addresses. The Integrator advised holding the baseline for a reference race, but I did not take that advice. The first race is already complete and shows the failure mode clearly, so holding would waste a race on a known-failing result. Instead I am taking the Integrator's second-stage change now, a wider span of ±0.03 m, and keeping the forward offset at 0.05 m so the effect can be attributed. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, a max_error below the off-track limit on at least some tracks, and higher progress. I am not changing the wheel track, mass, or body, because the evidence does not point at them. Body width does not help the off-track limit: with body_width 0.14 the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125+0.035) = 0.06 m, and it would need about 0.19 m before it rose above 0.06 m, outside the allowed range.
